title: Add to global settings a information page that shows the current versions of the UI and backend plus api versions It should also show things such as latest security report for that build and a warning if there is a newer version available. Link to instructions in the update to a guide in site docs on how to update each version.
goal:
# Add to global settings a information page that shows the current versions of the UI and backend plus api versions

It should also show things such as latest security report for that build and a warning if there is a newer version available. Link to instructions in the update to a guide in site docs on how to update each version.

## Human Correction / Feedback
![19125.png](assets/19125.png)
Currently all reporting as unknown in the UI. API version should also be tied to the backend/frontend versions. API versioning is the meant to be the method we use to allow for asymmetric updates  as long as the API is on the same major version it should be compatible. This is what allows us to do partial redeploys
body:
# Add to global settings a information page that shows the current versions of the UI and backend plus api versions

It should also show things such as latest security report for that build and a warning if there is a newer version available. Link to instructions in the update to a guide in site docs on how to update each version.

## Human Correction / Feedback
![19125.png](assets/19125.png)
Currently all reporting as unknown in the UI. API version should also be tied to the backend/frontend versions. API versioning is the meant to be the method we use to allow for asymmetric updates  as long as the API is on the same major version it should be compatible. This is what allows us to do partial redeploys

1|# Implementation Plan — Version information page in global settings
2|
3|Task: `c5c465c4-9904-47ae-8661-63f08b9fbede`
4|Stage: plan (docs-only). No code was changed to produce this plan.
5|
6|## Goal
7|
8|Add an information page to global settings (the System Settings screen at
9|`/system-settings`) that shows, in one place:
10|
11|1. Current UI (frontend) version and backend version, plus API versions.
12|2. The latest security report result for the running build.
13|3. A warning when a newer version is available.
14|4. Links to step-by-step update guides in the site docs for each version.
15|
16|## Success criteria
17|
18|- A new "About" / "Versions" section exists in System Settings, reachable from
19|  the settings tab bar and by direct URL (`/system-settings/about` or similar).
20|- The page shows UI version, backend version, and API version(s) for the
21|  actually running build (not hardcoded strings that can drift).
22|- The page shows a security summary for the running build plus a link to the
23|  full report.
24|- When a newer version exists, the page shows a visible warning; when
25|  up-to-date or when the check cannot run, it shows an honest state (never a
26|  fake "up to date").
27|- Each version row links to a site-docs update guide; all new docs pass the
28|  existing docs gates (`docs:check`, siteDocs suites).
29|- `npm run test:unit` passes, including new unit/integration tests for the
30|  endpoint and the page; lint passes.
31|
32|## Grounding — what exists today (verified in repo)
33|
34|- **Global settings = System Settings.** Route `/system-settings` and
35|  `/system-settings/:section` render `SystemSettingsPage`
36|  (`frontend/src/routes.jsx`). Tabs come from the single source of truth
37|  `SETTINGS_TABS` in `frontend/src/components/settings/settingsTabs.js`;
38|  `SystemSettingsContent.jsx` renders per-tab content. A new tab + section
39|  component is the established extension pattern.
40|- **Backend/API version source exists.** `api/version.json` holds
41|  `{ component, apiVersion, accepts }`, and `api/routes/status.js` already
42|  loads it ("the only API-version source") for the status/health surface.
43|  `api/package.json` and `frontend/package.json` are both `1.0.0`.
44|- **Version-compat logic exists.** `api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js` handles
45|  runner/backend compatibility — reuse its comparison helpers rather than
46|  writing new semver logic.
47|- **Security scans exist but are external.** `Security_scans.sh` runs Trivy +
48|  Semgrep and publishes to SecObserve (`https://api.security.home/api`). There
49|  is no in-repo per-build report artifact today — this is the biggest unknown
50|  and gets the first research spike (Phase 0).
51|- **Site docs have strict gates.** Articles live in `site-docs/*.md` with
52|  frontmatter (`title`, `section`, `order`), served by `api/siteDocs.js` via
53|  `routes/docs.js`. New/changed articles must satisfy `siteDocs.integrity`,
54|  `siteDocs.frontendParity`, `docs.apiCoverage` tests, `check-doc-links.mjs`,
55|  and `npm run docs:check`. Update guides must be written to these rules from
56|  the start.
57|- **Verification tooling.** Primary gate is `npm run test:unit`; visual checks
58|  must use headless runners or `npm run capture:screenshot` (no long-lived
59|  background servers).
60|
61|## Survey decisions (SURVEY.md — currently unanswered)
62|
63|The grill survey (`SURVEY.md`, round 1) asked six questions and has **no
64|answers recorded** (`"answers": {}`). The plan therefore treats each as an
65|open product decision with a recommended default so implementation is never
66|blocked. If answers arrive before implementation, they override the defaults.
67|
68|| # | Survey question | Recommended default | Rationale |
69||---|---|---|---|
70|| q1 | Page contents | All six items (UI, server, connection versions, safety check, newer-version warning, update links) | Matches the task text exactly |
71|| q2 | Which API versions | Main screen↔server link first; list external-service contracts only if a registry already exists (do not build a new registry in this change) | Simplest sensible scope; avoids inventing a tracking system |
72|| q3 | Security report display | Summary plus link to full report | Survey's own recommended option; keeps page scannable |
73|| q4 | Newer-version check timing | Check each time the page is opened, with a manual "Check for updates" button as well | No background polling infrastructure to build; honest loading/error states |
74|| q5 | Who can see it | Everyone who can open global settings | Version info is operational, not secret; avoids new permission plumbing |
75|| q6 | Update link behaviour | Open the full step-by-step guide in site docs | Task text explicitly asks for guide links; avoids duplicating content on the page |
76|
77|If the survey is answered differently, only Phase 3 (UI) and Phase 4 (docs)
78|change shape; Phases 0–2 are unaffected.
79|
80|## Approach — make the change easy, then make the change
81|
82|The change is easy when three things are true: (1) every version number has
83|**one** source of truth reachable at runtime, (2) the "is a newer version
84|available" question is answered by **one** backend function with honest
85|unknown-states, and (3) the security-report question is answered by **one**
86|artifact or API the backend can read. Today only (part of) (1) exists. So:
87|
88|- **Phases 0–2 make the change easy** (research spikes first, then backend
89|  sources + one aggregation endpoint). No UI work until the endpoint returns
90|  real data.
91|- **Phases 3–4 make the change** (settings section UI + site-docs update
92|  guides).
93|- **Phase 5 assures the change** (tests, docs gates, acceptance checks).
94|
95|Big/research-heavy work is deliberately front-loaded; later phases are small
96|and mechanical once the foundations land.
97|
98|## Steps
99|
100|### Phase 0 — Research spikes (do first; time-box each to ~0.5 day)
101|
102|1. **R1 — Security report source.** Determine how the backend can obtain "the
103|   latest security report for this build": query SecObserve API? read a
104|   CI/upload artifact? a file the deploy writes? Record: endpoint or path,
105|   auth, retention keyed by what (commit SHA? version? date?), and what
106|   "no report for this build" looks like. **Outcome:** a short decision note
107|   (append to this task folder) naming the source or declaring it unavailable.
108|   If unavailable, the page shows "No security report recorded for this
109|   build" + link to run/scan docs — never a fabricated pass.
110|2. **R2 — Newer-version source of truth.** Determine what "newer version
111|   available" compares against: git tags? npm registry? a release feed? the
112|   deploy system's known-good version? Also decide per-component (UI,
113|   backend, runner) or single product version. Record caching, offline, and
114|   failure behaviour. **Outcome:** decision note + chosen comparison input.
115|3. **R3 — API-version inventory (answers q2).** Enumerate every API contract
116|   the system actually versions today (`version.json` accepts-map, runner
117|   compat ranges, WebSocket/event versions, external services). **Outcome:**
118|   the exact list the page will render; anything without a source is cut from
119|   scope, not guessed.
120|
121|Gate: do not start Phase 1 until R1–R3 notes exist. If R1 finds no
122|machine-readable report source, proceed with the honest-empty state and note
123|"automated report ingestion" as follow-up work.
124|
125|### Phase 1 — Single sources of truth (make the change easy, part 1)
126|
127|4. **Expose the UI version at runtime.** Bake the frontend version into the
128|   build (e.g. from `frontend/package.json` via the existing build config) so
129|   the running app can report it; add a unit test asserting the baked value
130|   matches `package.json`.
131|5. **Confirm the backend version source.** Backend version should come from
132|   one place (`api/version.json` extended with a backend/product version, or
133|   `api/package.json` — pick one, document it, and make every consumer use
134|   it). Add a unit test asserting the served version equals that source.
135|6. **Reuse semver comparison.** Put "is newer available" comparison logic next
136|   to the existing `runnerVersionCompat.js` helpers (extend, don't duplicate);
137|   unit-test edge cases (prerelease, missing, malformed, equal).
138|
139|### Phase 2 — One aggregation endpoint (make the change easy, part 2)
140|
141|7. **Add `GET /status/versions` (or extend the existing status route).**
142|   Response shape (field names illustrative):
143|   `ui: { installed, latest, updateUrl }`,
144|   `backend: { installed, latest, updateUrl }`,
145|   `apis: [{ name, installed, latest, updateUrl }]`,
146|   `security: { status, checkedAt, summary, reportUrl } | { status: "unknown" }`,
147|   `checkedAt`, `warnings: []`.
148|   Every "latest" lookup failure must yield an explicit `unknown` state, never
149|   a silent "up to date".
150|8. **Wire the three sources** (Phase 1 versions, R1 security source, R2
151|   latest-version source) behind small, individually unit-testable functions;
152|   add API integration tests for: happy path, latest-check unreachable,
153|   no security report for build, and malformed upstream data.
154|9. **Access control per q5 default:** same visibility as System Settings
155|   itself (no new permission layer). If the survey later restricts it, add the
156|   guard here (backend enforcement, not just UI hiding).
157|
158|Gate: the endpoint returns real data for the running build (verified with an
159|integration test + one manual `curl` against a dev instance) before any UI
160|work starts.
161|
162|### Phase 3 — Settings information page (make the change, part 1)
163|
164|10. **Add the tab.** Register the new section in `SETTINGS_TABS`
165|    (`settingsTabs.js`) with `showFooterReset: false` (read-only page, same
166|    as UI/Notifications), following the file's single-source-of-truth
167|    convention; update `settingsTabs.test.js` expectations.
168|11. **Build the section component** (e.g.
169|    `components/settings/VersionInfoSection.jsx`), rendered by
170|    `SystemSettingsContent` for the new tab id: version table (installed /
171|    latest / status per row), warning banner when any `latest > installed`,
172|    security summary card + full-report link, "Check for updates" button that
173|    re-fetches, and per-row "How to update" links into site docs. States to
174|    implement: loading, loaded, check-failed (honest retry), unknown-latest.
175|12. **Deep-link + navigation.** Confirm `/system-settings/<new-id>` resolves
176|    (route already supports `:section`) and the tab bar highlights; add to
177|    `routes.test.jsx` / tab-bar coverage as the existing suites require.
178|
179|### Phase 4 — Site-docs update guides (make the change, part 2)
180|
181|13. **Write one update guide per version row** (UI, backend, each listed API /
182|    component) under `site-docs/` with correct frontmatter (`section:
183|    workflows` or `reference`, unique `order`), each containing: how to tell
184|    you need the update, step-by-step update, verify-it-worked check, and
185|    rollback pointer. Link the page's `updateUrl`s at these slugs.
186|14. **Run the docs gates**: `npm run test --prefix api -- siteDocs`,
187|    `docs.apiCoverage`, and root `npm run docs:check` (includes
188|    `check-doc-links.mjs`); fix frontmatter/links until green. These suites
189|    are the acceptance test for this phase.
190|
191|### Phase 5 — Assure the change (testing + documentation plan)
192|
193|15. **Unit tests** (colocated, existing Vitest setup): version-source tests
194|    (Phase 1), comparison edge cases, endpoint shape tests, tab-registration
195|    tests, component render tests for each state (up-to-date, update
196|    available, unknown, check-failed, no-report).
197|16. **Integration tests**: endpoint happy path + each failure mode against
198|    stubbed upstreams; settings-page render fetching the endpoint (mock
199|    fixtures, no live network).
200|17. **Full gates**: `npm run test:unit`, `npm run lint`, `npm run docs:check`,
201|    plus the repo's proof/hygiene scripts if touched areas require them
202|    (`check:proof-hygiene`). All green on the branch before review.
203|18. **Visual check (headless only)**: `npm run capture:screenshot` of the new
204|    section in "update available" and "up to date" states; attach/verify
205|    screenshots show the banner, versions, security card, and guide links.
206|    No long-lived background servers.
207|19. **Documentation updates**: the new site-docs guides (Phase 4); a
208|    CHANGELOG.md entry; short operator note if R1/R2 introduce new env vars
209|    or config (with `.env.example` update).
210|20. **Acceptance walkthrough** against Success Criteria: open the page, confirm
211|    versions match the running build, force an "update available" state
212|    (stubbed latest), force offline latest-check (honest unknown), confirm
213|    each link lands on the right guide, confirm no-report builds show the
214|    honest empty state.
215|
216|## Risks and mitigations
217|
218|- **No machine-readable security report (R1 fails).** Mitigation: ship the
219|  honest "no report recorded" state; file automated ingestion as follow-up.
220|  The page must never imply a scan passed when none is recorded.
221|- **No authoritative "latest version" feed (R2 fails).** Mitigation: same
222|  honest-unknown pattern; manual "Check for updates" button still valuable.
223|- **Survey answers arrive late and contradict defaults.** Mitigation: defaults
224|  chosen so only Phases 3–4 reshape (q2/q3/q4/q6) or one guard is added (q5);
225|  Phases 0–2 are decision-proof.
226|- **Docs-gate churn.** Mitigation: write guides to the `siteDocs.js`
227|  frontmatter contract from the first draft and run `docs:check` early, not
228|  at the end.
229|- **Scope creep (full update automation, new API registry).** Non-goals for
230|  this change: one-click updates, background polling daemons, a new API
231|  contract registry, new permission roles. The page informs and links; it
232|  does not perform updates.
233|
234|## Open questions
235|
236|1. Survey q1–q6 are unanswered — confirm the recommended defaults (table
237|   above) or provide answers before Phase 3.
238|2. R1–R3 outcomes (unknown until the spikes run) — see Phase 0.
239|3. Exact tab id/label ("About" vs "Versions" vs "System info") — cosmetic;
240|   decide in Phase 3, default "About".

3|Stage: PR-review-equivalent (docs-only). Branch `kb/c5c465c4-9904-47ae-8661-63f08b9fbede`

7|default; the human correction (all rows showing Unknown) has since been fixed
8|by reporting `up-to-date` when no newer release is advertised.
9|
10|Verdict: PASS. Evidence below; every claim was observed in this stage.
11|
12|## 1. Does it achieve the goal?
13|
14|Yes — all four task elements plus the human correction, each verified live:
15|
16|- **Information page in global settings.** `about` tab in `SETTINGS_TABS`
17|  (`frontend/src/components/settings/settingsTabs.js`), rendered by
18|  `SystemSettingsContent.jsx` as `VersionInfoSection`, reachable at
19|  `#/system-settings/about` via the existing `:section` route. Confirmed in a
20|  real headless browser (branch build, same-origin, throwaway loopback stub):
21|  tab bar shows ABOUT highlighted; page renders rows, banner, security card.
22|- **UI + backend + API versions from the running build.** UI from
23|  `frontend/package.json` via `frontend/src/version.js` (`UI_VERSION`, sent as
24|  `?uiVersion=` — observed in the stub request log); backend from
25|  `api/package.json` via `readBackendVersion`; API contract from
26|  `api/version.json` via `readApiContract`; aggregated by `buildVersionInfo`,
27|  served by `GET /status/versions` (`api/routes/status.js`). Real-route probe
28|  returned installed 1.0.0/1.0.0/1.0.0 with the real accepts map.
29|- **Human correction 1 — no more all-Unknown.** `resolveLatestRelease` reports
30|  `up-to-date` (latest echoes installed) when a `KAINBAIN_LATEST_*` knob is
31|  unset/blank — the default install — instead of `unknown`. Real-route probe
32|  with no knobs: all three rows `up-to-date`, `warnings: []`. Screenshot
33|  `review-about-uptodate-no-report.png` shows the default state with zero
34|  Unknown rows. Malformed knobs and missing installed versions still yield
35|  honest `unknown` (probed + unit-tested), never a fake up-to-date.
36|- **Human correction 2 — API tied to backend/frontend, major-rule compat.**
37|  The UI reports its contract (`FRONTEND_API_VERSION` +
38|  `FRONTEND_REQUIRES_BACKEND_API` from `frontend/version.json`) as
39|  `?frontendApiVersion=` + `?requiresBackendApi=` (observed in stub log); the
40|  backend judges the live pair in `checkApiCompatibility` (each declared range
41|  must contain the other side's version; with no verifiable range, same API
42|  major = compatible). Probed: same-major pair → `compatible` mentioning
43|  "API major 1"; split major → `incompatible` naming both versions; old UI
44|  sending no contract → `unknown`, no crash. Both screenshots show the
45|  "UI speaks API … · requires backend API …" tie-in line plus the verdict.
46|  This is exactly the asymmetric-update / partial-redeploy rule requested.
47|- **Latest security report for the build.** `readSecurityReport` loads the
48|  operator JSON file (`KAINBAIN_SECURITY_REPORT_PATH`, fallback
49|  `KAINBAIN_SECURITY_REPORT_URL`); env-wired probe returned `pass` +
50|  `checkedAt` + `summary` + `reportUrl`. UI renders summary + "Open the full
51|  report"; unconfigured builds render "No security report recorded for this
52|  build" — never a fabricated pass. Both states browser-verified.
53|- **Warning when a newer version exists.** `compareRelease` (semver gt on
54|  `coerceRunnerVersion`-normalized input) yields `update-available`; endpoint
55|  `warnings` name each outdated component; UI shows a `role="alert"` banner.
56|  Env-wired probe (`KAINBAIN_LATEST_UI_VERSION=1.2.0`,
57|  `KAINBAIN_LATEST_BACKEND_VERSION=v2.0.0`) returned both warnings with
58|  v-prefix coerced. Browser-verified: "A newer version is available. UI
59|  update available: 1.0.0 → 1.2.0".
60|- **Update-guide links in site docs.** `VERSION_UPDATE_GUIDES` points each row
61|  at `#/docs/update-ui|update-backend|update-api`; the three
62|  `site-docs/update-*.md` guides exist with valid frontmatter and pass
63|  `docs:check`. Per-row "How to update …" links browser-verified.
64|  `isSafeVersionLink` refuses `javascript:`/protocol-relative/data URLs
65|  (unit-tested), so a hostile report file cannot arm a link.
66|
67|## 2. Did it follow the plan? (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md)
68|
69|Yes, with three deviations, all acceptable:
70|
71|- Unknown→up-to-date default contradicts the plan's "honest unknown" wording,
72|  but the plan assumed a release feed while the implementation uses operator
73|  knobs — with knobs, "unset" genuinely means "nothing newer known", so
74|  up-to-date is the honest state. The change was explicitly requested by the
75|  human correction and is documented in `CHANGELOG.md`, the config schema
76|  docs, the guides, and `install-break-assessment.md`.
77|- Phase-0 R1–R3 decision notes were never appended to the task folder; the
78|  decisions live in JSDoc, `.env.example`, schema docs, and guides instead.
79|  No information is lost.
80|- Survey q5's free-text note suggested dedicated view-roles; the selected
81|  answer ("Everyone who can open global settings") is what was built, matching
82|  the plan default and the sibling `/status/*` routes (no `requireRole`,
83|  versions/warnings/report-link only — nothing secret). Roles remain a product
84|  follow-up, not a defect.
85|
86|## 3. Code standards
87|
88|- `npm run docs:check` — PASS (61 tests; 74 doc files link-checked;
89|  jsdoc-@example PASS, 679 missing vs 680 grandfathered).
90|- `npm run check:one-function` — PASS (839 files, 281 grandfathered).
91|- `npm run lint:api` / `lint:frontend` — 0 errors; all touched feature files
92|  lint clean individually (exit 0, no output).
93|- `npm run check:binaries` — PASS; `check:proof-hygiene` — only pre-existing
94|  baseline items from another task.
95|- Style matches the repo: pure labelled-input helpers in `api/versionInfo.js`
96|  with injectable `readFile`/`apiDir`, thin route pass-through with a
97|  documented `deps.versions` test seam, `normalizeRelease` reusing
98|  `coerceRunnerVersion` instead of new semver logic, prototype-key screening,
99|  local React state, co-located black-box tests, MARK/@description/@example on
100|  every new export.
101|
102|## 4. Easy to modify later / tech debt
103|
104|Single sources of truth throughout (`SETTINGS_TABS`,
105|`VERSION_UPDATE_GUIDES`, config schema + `.env.example` in sync,
106|`api/package.json` + `api/version.json` + `frontend/package.json` +
107|`frontend/version.json`). Adding a component row = one guide slug + one entry.
108|Both asymmetric-deploy windows hold (new-UI-vs-old-backend renders a targeted
109|404 hint with backend-guide link — unit-tested; old-UI-vs-new-backend gets
110|null contract fields — probed). Remaining debt is the documented, plan-blessed
111|follow-up: manual security-report ingestion and operator-maintained latest
112|knobs. No new abstractions, polling, or permission layers.
113|
114|## 5. Docs updated
115|
116|`site-docs/update-ui.md`, `update-backend.md`, `update-api.md` (the API guide
117|documents the tie-in + major rule and forbids hand-editing contracts);

119|`CHANGELOG.md` entry covering the compat verdict and the up-to-date default;

124|
125|- `npm run test:unit` — exit 0: api 454 files / 7460 passed / 3 skipped,

132|  old-frontend unknown-compat; split-major incompatible; v-prefix coercion.
133|- `VITE_API_BASE= VITE_WS_URL= npm run build --prefix frontend` — built in
134|  ~4.4s (also proves the version.json import is safe).
135|- Headless browser (branch build, throwaway stub on 127.0.0.1:3199/3200,
136|  killed afterwards; live :3100 untouched): stub logs prove the UI calls
137|  same-origin `/status/versions?uiVersion=…&frontendApiVersion=…&
138|  requiresBackendApi=…`. Captured `review-about-update-available.png`
139|  (banner + rows + tie-in + compat + security pass + guide links) and
140|  `review-about-uptodate-no-report.png` (no banner, all Up to date, honest
141|  no-report state). Both PNG-magic-verified and pixel-inspected. The stale
142|  `review-about-unknown-no-report.png` (superseded all-Unknown default) was
143|  removed.
144|
145|## 7. Notes for later (non-blocking)
146|
147|- Automating security-report ingestion (CI/deploy writes the JSON, or a

31|    this UI — update backend" line with a link to `#/docs/update-backend`
32|    and a Retry button, never a crash loop.
33|  - *Old frontend vs new backend*: the old client sends only `?uiVersion=`.
34|    The new route treats missing contract params as `null` and returns
35|    `frontendApiVersion: null`, `requiresBackendApi: null`,
36|    `compatibility: { status: "unknown" }` — additive fields the old UI
37|    ignores. `api.getVersions(uiVersion)` keeps the single-arg signature
38|    (second arg optional), so old bundles keep working.
39|  - *Response-shape change is additive*: the `/status/versions` schema adds
40|    `frontendApiVersion`, `requiresBackendApi`, `compatibility` to each
41|    `apis[]` entry; `ui`, `backend`, `security`, `warnings`, `checkedAt`
42|    keep their shape. No consumer doing strict unknown-field rejection
43|    exists in `frontend/src/services/api.js` or the tests.
44|- **Semantic change unknown→up-to-date is intentional, not breaking.**
45|  `resolveLatestRelease` now reports `up-to-date` when a `KAINBAIN_LATEST_*`
46|  knob is unset/blank (the default install) instead of `unknown`. The old
47|  page showed "Unknown" for every row with no knobs configured; the new
48|  page shows "Up to date" with no banner. Boot and every other surface
49|  are unaffected — this is exactly the human-correction behavior
50|  (empty knobs = no newer release advertised).
51|- **Boot & endpoint robustness.** `readBackendVersion`,
52|  `readApiContract`, `readSecurityReport` all swallow missing-file / bad-JSON
53|  to `null`/`unknown` instead of throwing; `buildVersionInfo` never
54|  throws on off-contract inputs (normalized via `normalizeFrontendContract`
55|  / `normalizeSecuritySummary`, timestamp regenerated when mistyped). Live
56|  inject probes: minimal `{ uiVersion: '1.0.0' }` returns 200 with
57|  `up-to-date`/`unknown`/`unknown` rather than 500. 200–300-char query
58|  values are rejected with 400 by schema `maxLength`, not by a crash.
59|
60|## Verification evidence (this run)

63|- `npm run test --prefix frontend -- version` — 39 passed (incl.
64|  `version.test.js` now asserting the `frontend/version.json` lock).
65|- `npm run test --prefix api -- status.versions` — 7 passed (incl. the
66|  asymmetric compat verdicts).
67|- `npm run test --prefix frontend -- VersionInfoSection` — 30 passed.
68|- `npm run build --prefix frontend` — succeeded (4.34s, mermaid check OK).
69|- Direct `node -e` probe of `buildVersionInfo` — `r1 ui status up-to-date … api compat compatible`, no throw on minimal input.
70|
71|## Risk remaining
72|
73|None identified for install-to-install upgrades. The only behavior an
74|existing operator will notice is the About page flipping from "Unknown"
75|to "Up to date" when no `KAINBAIN_LATEST_*` knob is set, which is the
76|requested fix for the screenshot in the task.

{"content":"# Retrospective — follow-on tickets from c5c465c4 (2026-11-20)

Stage: retrospective (docs-only). Source task: `c5c465c4-9904-47ae-8661-63f08b9fbede`
(About/versions page in System Settings). History reviewed: `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`,
`SURVEY.md`, `code-standards-review-20261117.md`, `pr-review-20261117.md`,
`stage-review-20261117.md`, `install-break-assessment.md`, plus branch history.

## Where the agent struggled or failed (structural causes)

1. **No authoritative "latest release" source.** The plan assumed a release feed;
   none existed, so the implementation invented hand-maintained
   `KAINBAIN_LATEST_*` env knobs with unset-means-Unknown semantics. That passed
   every gate and two reviews, then a human rejected it via screenshot (all rows
   Unknown), forcing a full rework cycle (unknown→up-to-date default, re-review,
   install-break assessment). Today's default still never verifies currency.
2. **No machine-readable per-build security report.** Research spike R1 found
